clips.text_zh: 我喺2024年11月高位將全副身家溝落MSTR。兩年慢慢流走晒。每一個小升浪畀我一絲希望，第二日就跌。每次「向下加倉」，都跌得更深。我只想攞返啲錢。依家輸咗70,000美元。我真係唔知點可以 financially recover。
clips.text_en_b1: I aped my life savings into MSTR at the top in November 2024. For two years, my entire net worth slowly bled out. Every small pump gave me a little hope, then it dumped the next day. Every time I averaged down, it dropped even more. I just want some of my money back. I am down $70,000 and may never financially recover.
clips.source_hint: A trader describes two years of losses after buying MSTR at its November 2024 high.

signal.rationale: This is pure loss-pain storytelling with no actionable trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: I put my entire life savings into MSTR at the peak in November 2024, and over the following two years, my net worth slowly bled out. Every minor rally offered a glimmer of hope, but the stock dumped the next day. Whenever I averaged down, it fell even further, turning each attempt to rescue my position into a deeper loss. At this point, I simply want to recover some of my money.
clips.text_en_c1: I aped my entire life savings into MSTR at the peak in November 2024, and for the past two years my net worth has slowly bled away. Every minor pump offered a glimmer of hope, only for the stock to dump the following day. Averaging down merely made the position worse, since each decline took me deeper underwater. At this stage, I am no longer focused on getting rich; I simply want to recover some of my money. I am already down $70,000, and there is a real possibility that I will never financially recover from this mistake.
clips.text_en_c2: I aped my entire life savings into MSTR at the November 2024 high, and over the following two years my net worth slowly bled out. Every minor rally offered a fleeting glimmer of hope, only for the stock to dump the following day; whenever I averaged down, it fell even further. I have watched repeated attempts to rescue the position culminate in deeper losses, and all I want now is to recover some of my money. I am down $70,000 and genuinely do not know how I will financially recover. If anyone has advice, please send it my way.

clips.text_zh: 「JAI HIND INDIA SUPERPOWER 2030。」帖主話印度有世界最好嘅人口結構、教育同科技產業，又鄰近Persian Gulf，天然有油氣供應。中國一弱，製造產業可能畀印度吸走。中俄如果崩，印度更加可以控制Eurasian continental landmass。
clips.text_en_b1: JAI HIND INDIA SUPERPOWER 2030. The post says India has the world's best demographics, a strong education system, and a major technology sector. It also sits near the Persian Gulf, so oil and gas should be secure. As China weakens, India could absorb its manufacturing sector.
clips.source_hint: An optimistic post argues that India could become a superpower by 2030.

signal.rationale: Non-trading geopolitical commentary with no market setup

clips.text_en_b2: “JAI HIND INDIA SUPERPOWER 2030.” The post argues that India has the world’s best demographics, a strong education system, and a major technology industry. Its proximity to the Persian Gulf also gives it relatively secure access to oil and gas. As China weakens, some of its manufacturing sector could be absorbed by India. Furthermore, if China and Russia collapse, India may gain control over much of the Eurasian continental landmass, giving it extraordinary strategic power.
clips.text_en_c1: 'JAI HIND INDIA SUPERPOWER 2030.' The poster argues that India possesses the world's strongest demographic structure, a robust education system, and a major technology industry. Its proximity to the Persian Gulf also provides natural access to oil and gas supplies. If China continues to weaken, India could absorb much of its manufacturing capacity. Furthermore, should China and Russia collapse, India would be well placed to exert considerable influence across the Eurasian continental landmass. The post presents these advantages as the foundation of India's emergence as a global superpower by 2030.
clips.text_en_c2: “JAI HIND INDIA SUPERPOWER 2030.” The poster argues that India possesses the world's strongest demographic profile, a robust education system, and a thriving technology industry. Its proximity to the Persian Gulf also provides comparatively secure access to oil and gas, giving it resources that many rival economies lack. As China's relative decline continues, India could attract a substantial share of manufacturing capacity now moving away from Chinese supply chains. Furthermore, should China and Russia experience serious instability, India would be well placed to exert considerable influence across the Eurasian continental landmass. The claim is obviously bullish, but the underlying strategic advantages are difficult to dismiss.

clips.text_zh: 「點解fat people以為食肉健康？」帖主話，Annals of Internal Medicine一系列研究發現，少食紅肉同加工肉，同較低總死亡率、較低心血管病死亡率有統計顯著關係。靠戒maintenance唔係ego，係body check。
clips.text_en_b1: Why do fat people think meat is healthy when the science shows it is unhealthy? The post says studies in the Annals of Internal Medicine found significantly lower total and cardiovascular mortality among people eating less red and processed meat. Fat people being angry about this is predictable, but the evidence still matters.
clips.source_hint: A fitness thread attacks the idea that red meat is healthy and cites mortality studies.

signal.rationale: Non-trading fitness and nutrition discussion with no market setup

clips.text_en_b2: “Why do fat people think eating meat is healthy?” The post points to a series of studies in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which found statistically significant associations between eating less red and processed meat and lower overall mortality, including cardiovascular deaths. Although people may dislike being challenged, dismissing the evidence because it questions their identity does not change the findings. Cutting back for maintenance is not about ego; it is simply paying attention to what the body needs.
clips.text_en_c1: 'Why do fat people think eating meat is healthy when the science shows the opposite?' The post cites a series of studies published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which found statistically significant associations between eating less red and processed meat and lower overall mortality, including reduced cardiovascular mortality. Whether anyone finds this conclusion unwelcome is largely beside the point. Maintaining personal health is not an exercise in ego, however uncomfortable the evidence may be; it is a routine check on what the body is telling us. The findings warrant attention rather than reflexive denial.
clips.text_en_c2: “Why do fat people think eating meat is healthy?” The poster points to a series of studies published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, which found that lower consumption of red and processed meat was statistically associated with lower overall mortality and cardiovascular mortality. The implication is stark: reducing meat is not merely an exercise in maintaining one's physique or appeasing an inflated ego, but a legitimate health precaution grounded in epidemiological evidence. People who feel personally challenged by the findings may respond with predictable anger, yet emotional discomfort does not alter the data. If diet influences long-term mortality, defending an unhealthy pattern on personal grounds is an extraordinarily weak argument.

clips.text_en_b1: Every /biz/ anon thinks he is the next Michael Burry after watching a 17-minute YouTube video about credit spreads. He draws a red triangle on TradingView and says, “THE EVERYTHING BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO POP.” He has predicted 38 of the last two recessions, while the S&P dropped 0.4% on Friday.
clips.source_hint: The post mocks amateur market doomsters who call every bubble the next big collapse.

signal.rationale: The post mocks bearish predictions but gives no clear entry, target, or stop

clips.text_en_b2: Every /biz/ anonymous poster thinks he is the next Michael Burry after watching a 17-minute YouTube video about credit spreads. He draws a red triangle on TradingView and announces, “THE EVERYTHING BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO POP.” The story claims that a FRED chart predicted 38 recessions, although the S&P actually fell by only 0.4% on Friday. It is a perfect example of confident market commentary that sounds precise while remaining completely disconnected from reality.
clips.text_en_c1: Every /biz/ anonymous poster believes he is the next Michael Burry after watching a 17-minute YouTube video about credit spreads. He then draws a red triangle on TradingView and declares, 'THE EVERYTHING BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO POP.' His forecasting record is rather less impressive than his confidence: the story claims that he has successfully predicted 38 of the previous two recessions. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 fell by 0.4% on Friday. The contrast between dire predictions and an ordinary market session neatly captures the kind of confident amateur analysis that regularly circulates online.
clips.text_en_c2: Every anonymous poster on /biz/ fancies himself the next Michael Burry after watching a 17-minute YouTube video on credit spreads. He draws a red triangle on TradingView, announces with theatrical certainty that “THE EVERYTHING BUBBLE IS ABOUT TO POP,” and treats a chart resembling a bearish flag as financial insight. His forecasting record is, to put it generously, unconventional: he has supposedly predicted 38 of the last two recessions, an achievement that neatly demonstrates the difficulty of calling a collapse before it occurs. Meanwhile, the S&P fell by 0.4% on Friday, presumably far less dramatic than his imminent apocalypse. Confidence, in this forum, remains comfortably detached from calibration.
